reasons: The cited § 7.2 obligation — Customer must disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider — is a right-of-first-refusal that conditions our freedom to buy elsewhere, so it falls squarely within the exclusivity/restrictive-covenant rule as a deviation from the preferred 'no exclusivity obligation on Customer' position.

The redline deletes only p0026, which is the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position; no exclusivity running in Customer's favour is disturbed, and the deterministic checks confirm no residual requirements/sole-supplier obligation.

The comment is accurate and correctly tied to the drafting: it explains the de facto exclusivity effect, cites the internal contradiction with § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement of no exclusivity or MFC commitment), and offers the playbook fallback (defined category, ≤12 months, automatic exit on service-level/delivery failure) in the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
Cross-references are handled correctly: the § 2.1 take-or-pay volume commitment is flagged as context only and expressly left to the minimum-commitment rule, avoiding scope creep in this finding.
